ei.title: Choose Readers for Critical Insight, Not Closeness
ei.subject: 9월_2026 고2 모의고사
ei.lesson: Choose Readers for Critical Insight, Not Closeness

fullPassage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most (A)[valuable / worthless] feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are (B)[awful / ideal], but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been (C)[useless / helpful] ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① valuable — ideal — helpful: 원문 그대로 ← 정답

❌ ② worthless(가치 없는)는 valuable의 반의어라 '가장 값진 피드백'이라는 흐름과 반대

❌ ③ awful(끔찍한)은 '동료 작가가 이상적'이라는 긍정 맥락과 반대

❌ ④ useless(쓸모없는)는 '도움이 된' 의견이라는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: the most valuable feedback / writers are ideal / opinions have been helpful

questions.passage: Only when you're (A)[happy / worried] that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your (B)[farthest / nearest] and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you (C)[despise / admire], and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① worried(걱정하는)는 '최선을 다해 만족할 때'라는 조건과 반대

❌ ② farthest(가장 먼)는 nearest(가장 가까운)의 반의어

✅ ③ happy — nearest — admire: 원문 그대로 ← 정답

❌ ④ despise(경멸하다)는 admire(존경하다)의 반의어라 '글을 존경하는 사람'이라는 흐름과 반대
det.tip: when you're happy / your nearest and dearest / whose writing you admire

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the (A)[best / worst] you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's (B)[terrible / fine], but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their (C)[trivial / critical] insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① worst(최악)는 '최선을 다했을 때'라는 흐름과 반대

❌ ② terrible(끔찍한)은 '그래도 괜찮다'는 fine과 반대

❌ ③ trivial(하찮은)은 critical(예리한 통찰)과 반대라 '예리한 통찰을 위해 독자를 고르라'는 요지와 어긋남

✅ ④ best — fine — critical: 원문 그대로 ← 정답
det.tip: done the best you can / that's fine / their critical insight

questions.passage: Only when you're ①<u>happy</u> that you've done the ②<u>worst</u> you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most ③<u>valuable</u> feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been ④<u>helpful</u> ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① happy(만족하는): '이야기에 최선을 다해 만족할 때'로 적절

❌ ② worst(최악의): '최악을 다했을 때 보여줘라'는 말이 되어 문맥상 부적절. 원래는 best(최선)여야 함 ← 정답

✅ ③ valuable(가치 있는): '가장 값진 피드백'으로 적절

✅ ④ helpful(도움이 되는): '도움이 된 의견'으로 적절
det.tip: you've done the best you can → best(최선)가 맞음

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you ①<u>show</u> it to someone else. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been ④<u>useless</u> ― and whose have not.

det.analysis:
✅ ① show(보여주다): '남에게 보여줘라'로 적절

✅ ② fine(괜찮은): '그것도 괜찮다'로 적절

✅ ③ insight(통찰): '비판적 통찰'로 적절

❌ ④ useless(쓸모없는): 뒤에 '어떤 의견은 그렇지 않았다(도움이 안 됐다)'와 대조되므로 여기는 helpful(도움이 되는)이어야 함 ← 정답
det.tip: opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not (도움이 된 것 ↔ 아닌 것 대조)

✅ ③ valuable(가치 있는): '가장 값진 피드백'으로 적절

det.analysis:
✅ ① sources(출처): '가장 값진 피드백은 다른 출처에서 나온다'로 이어지고, 콜론 뒤에서 '독자를 골라라'로 그 출처를 설명하므로 적절 ← 정답

❌ ② stories(이야기들): 피드백이 '이야기'에서 온다는 것은 어색

❌ ③ secrets(비밀들): 문맥과 무관

❌ ④ rules(규칙들): 문맥과 무관

det.analysis:
❌ ① useless(쓸모없는): '그러나 아무 작가나 되는 건 아니다'라는 단서로 보아 앞은 긍정이어야 함

❌ ② absent(없는): 문맥과 무관

✅ ③ ideal(이상적인): '동료 작가가 이상적이다, 그러나 아무 작가나 되는 건 아니다'로 자연스러움 ← 정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ideal와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
밑줄 친 ideal은 '가장 알맞은, 이상적인'이라는 뜻.

❌ ① terrible(끔찍한): 반대 의미

❌ ② ordinary(평범한): 의미가 다름

❌ ③ rare(드문): 의미가 다름

✅ ④ perfect(완벽한, 더할 나위 없는): ideal과 가장 가까움 ← 정답
det.tip: ideal ≒ perfect (더할 나위 없는)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. det.analysis:
밑줄 친 admire는 '~을 높이 평가하고 존경하다'라는 뜻.

❌ ① dislike(싫어하다): 반대 의미

❌ ② ignore(무시하다): 반대에 가까움

✅ ③ respect(존중하다): admire와 가장 가까움 ← 정답

❌ ④ forget(잊다): 의미가 다름
det.tip: admire ≒ respect (높이 평가하다)

det.analysis:
밑줄 친 helpful은 '도움이 되는, 유익한'이라는 뜻.

✅ ① useful(유용한): helpful과 가장 가까움 ← 정답

❌ ② useless(쓸모없는): 반대 의미

❌ ③ boring(지루한): 의미가 다름

❌ ④ simple(단순한): 의미가 다름
det.tip: helpful ≒ useful (유익한)

You may well want to show it to your <u>nearest</u> and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. det.analysis:
밑줄 친 nearest는 '가장 가까운'이라는 뜻.

❌ ① closest(가장 가까운): nearest와 같은 뜻(동의어 함정)

✅ ② farthest(가장 먼): nearest와 반대 ← 정답

❌ ③ dearest(가장 소중한): 거리가 아닌 애정의 축이라 반의어가 아님

❌ ④ quickest(가장 빠른): 속도의 축이라 무관
det.tip: nearest(가까운) ↔ farthest(먼)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. The most <u>valuable</u> feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 valuable와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
밑줄 친 valuable은 '가치 있는, 소중한'이라는 뜻.

❌ ① precious(귀중한): valuable과 같은 뜻(동의어 함정)

❌ ② expensive(비싼): 가격의 축이라 반의어가 아님

✅ ③ worthless(가치 없는): valuable과 반대 ← 정답

❌ ④ rare(드문): 희소성의 축이라 무관
det.tip: valuable(가치 있는) ↔ worthless(가치 없는)

questions.passage:
(A) I don't have a blue pen, but this black one will <u>do</u> for signing the form. Any simple tool is fine as long as it works.
(B) She has a lot of household chores to <u>do</u> before her guests arrive tonight. She wants everything to be perfect.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 do의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① (A)의 do는 '하다'가 아님

❌ ② (A)의 do는 '만들다'가 아님

❌ ③ (B)의 do는 '만들다'가 아님

✅ ④ (A) will do = '(그것이면) 충분하다/족하다', (B) chores to do = '(집안일을) 하다' ← 정답
det.tip: 본문 'any writer will do'의 do도 (A)처럼 '충분하다/적합하다'의 뜻

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "helpful information or criticism about your work, given to help you improve it"

det.analysis:
정의: '너의 작업에 대해 개선을 돕도록 주어지는 유익한 정보나 비평'

❌ ① silence(침묵): 정보를 주는 것이 아님

✅ ② feedback(피드백): 정의와 정확히 일치 ← 정답

❌ ③ payment(지불): 무관

❌ ④ summary(요약): 개선을 돕는 비평이 아님
det.tip: feedback = 개선을 위한 유익한 의견·비평

questions.passage: If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose __________ (opinion) have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 빈칸 뒤 동사가 have(복수 동사)이고 '어떤 의견들이 도움이 되었는지'라는 복수 개념이므로, opinion을 복수형 opinions로 바꿔야 한다. whose opinions have been helpful.
det.tip: have been과 수 일치 → opinion → opinions(복수)

questions.passage: The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their __________ (close) to you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 빈칸 자리는 'their ___ to you'로 소유격 뒤 명사가 와야 한다. 형용사 close(가까운)를 명사형 closeness(가까움)로 바꾼다. '비판적 통찰'(critical insight, 명사)과 대구를 이루므로 명사형이 맞다.
det.tip: 형용사 close → 명사 closeness (-ness 붙여 명사화)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your nearest and dearest, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their __________, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 'not their closeness(가까움이 아니라)'와 대조되는 긍정적 기준이 필요하다.

✅ ① critical insight(예리한 통찰): '가까움이 아니라 예리한 통찰을 기준으로 독자를 고르라'로 자연스러움 ← 정답

❌ ② personal closeness(개인적 친밀함): 바로 뒤 closeness와 중복·모순

❌ ③ daily routine(일상): 무관

❌ ④ deep affection(깊은 애정): 가까움과 비슷해 대조가 안 됨
det.tip: for their ___, not their closeness (통찰 ↔ 가까움 대조)

questions.passage: Only when you're happy that you've done the best you can for your story should you show it to someone else. You may well want to show it to your __________, and that's fine, but in most cases you shouldn't look to their reading for any great benefit to your work. The most valuable feedback is likely to come from other sources: you should choose readers for their critical insight, not their closeness to you. Fellow writers are ideal, but don't imagine that any writer will do. If you are part of a writers' circle or class, you'll know whose writing you admire, and if you've had feedback in the past you'll know whose opinions have been helpful ― and whose have not.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: nearest and dearest = 가장 가깝고 소중한 사람들(가족·친구)
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤 '그것도 괜찮지만, 그들의 읽기에서 큰 도움을 기대하지는 말라'는 흐름이므로, 빈칸은 '보여주고 싶지만 비평엔 한계가 있는 가까운 사람들'이어야 한다.

❌ ① fellow writers(동료 작가): 뒤에서 '이상적'이라 추천되는 대상이라 상반됨

✅ ② nearest and dearest(가장 가깝고 소중한 사람들): 보여주고 싶지만 큰 도움은 기대 말라는 대상과 일치 ← 정답

❌ ③ critical readers(비판적 독자): 오히려 추천되는 대상

❌ ④ writing class(글쓰기 수업): 마지막 문장에 나오는 유익한 집단
det.tip: show it to your ___, that's fine, but…little benefit
